name: live
description: GPT Live voice coworker: the microphone, the speaker and the session live in this process, and what is said becomes work on this machine.

live.description: The running voice coworker: {op} with status, conversations, open, voice, state, context, agents, attach, delegate, watch, reply, note or cancel and the fields the op names.

tool.live.description: The voice coworker as a tool: {op} describe or call, with the live operation as `input`.

tool.live_note.description: Save a durable note or written result in the current voice conversation.

tool.live_agent.description: Spawn, list, inspect or cancel work started from the voice conversation.

dir.doc: Where the conversation record is written. `:memory:` keeps it in memory.

cwd.doc: Working directory the service and its agents resolve against.

duplex.doc: Keep listening while the assistant speaks, so the user can interrupt. Set it with headphones; on a speaker the microphone hears the assistant and answers itself.

credentials.doc: Where the OpenAI key is looked for when the environment does not carry one. Match the router's own credential directory.

provider.doc: Which transport carries a voice session. `gpt` dials GPT Live over the network; `local` runs the whole session in this process, through `stt`, `brain` and `tts`, and reaches the network only if one of those settings names an `http(s)://` endpoint. An unknown value fails `voice` rather than falling back.

models.doc: Where `stt` and `tts` resolve a bare filename. Used only when `provider` is `local`.

stt.doc: Speech-to-text for the local transport: a model filename resolved under `models`, or a literal `http(s)://` endpoint standing in for it until a sibling cartridge adds the runtime. Used only when `provider` is `local`.

tts.doc: Text-to-speech for the local transport: a model filename resolved under `models`, or a literal `http(s)://` endpoint standing in for it until a sibling cartridge adds the runtime. Used only when `provider` is `local`.

brain.doc: The OpenAI-shaped chat/completions endpoint the local transport asks for a reply, dialled with a bounded timeout so an endpoint that never answers closes the session instead of hanging the turn. Used only when `provider` is `local`.

greeting.doc: Greet the user out loud when a voice session opens, so the speaker proves itself before anything is asked of it.
